name: MiniCPM5-2B

lineage.how_derived: base training (stable + decay), mid-training, then post-training: 400B tokens of deep-thinking SFT, RL teachers per domain (critic-based algorithm of JustRL II), and on-policy distillation (OPD) merging 16 expert models (5 agentic)

purpose: The builder states it is built for on-device and local deployment in resource-constrained settings: local assistants, coding agents, tool-use workflows and reasoning where a compact model is preferred, with native long context. The open data (UltraData family) is released alongside.

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Card tag apache-2.0; the LICENSE text itself was not opened (the repo has no LICENSE file in the sibling list checked).

architecture.attention: GQA, 16 Q heads / 2 KV heads, head dim 128, full attention
architecture.drafter: separate DSpark drafter (openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B-DSpark, 0.65 GB, with a GGUF variant)
architecture.why_this_design: The card says it scales up the MiniCPM5-1B recipe to a plain Llama-architecture 2B for on-device use; it gives no reasoning for depth or GQA ratio. Emphasis is on data (UltraData tiered data management) and post-training.

engine_support.notes: Plain Llama architecture, so any Llama-capable engine (Tona's dense path included) loads it; official GGUF exists. The card does not list SGLang or vLLM versions.

strengths: Vendor numbers above same-size and several 4B models on coding, math, long context and tool use
Tiny: 1.6 GB at Q4_K_M, runs CPU-only (a user measured Q3 to Q8 throughput on a 2016 i3 laptop CPU)
Plain Llama architecture, simple to support and to speculate with (DSpark)
weaknesses: Terminal-Bench 8.6 against 25.8 for Qwen3.5-4B (vendor table): weak on long terminal agent work
Two users report degraded answers and refusals once function tools are supplied; chat template bugs with string tool-call arguments (open discussions)
soft.behavior: Deep-thinking (long chain of thought) model after SFT/RL/OPD. A user complains that with tools attached the model skips tools that do not match and gives up.

user_reports.summary: Several Chinese-language reports: answer quality and world knowledge collapse when function tools are added; the model gives up when no matching tool exists
'Exceptionally good for its size'; asks for a 48B-A4B MoE
Chat template crashes on string tool-call arguments and writes non-string values as Python repr

soft.maturity: OpenBMB has shipped MiniCPM since 2024 with a steady cadence; 949k downloads of the BF16 repo and 633k of the GGUF within 10 weeks; active discussion section (29 threads).

tona_fit.reason: Standard Llama architecture, permissive license and strong vendor numbers per size, but 2.5B parameters is below what a coding-agent worker needs, and terminal-agent results are weak. Useful as a draft or sub-agent model; no independent evidence yet.
blockers: tool-use behavior reports and template bugs

sources.note: discussion text via the HF API; Chinese threads read in outline

open_questions: Independent coding or agent evaluation (all numbers are vendor-run; some scores marked as taken from other reports)
Real DSpark speed-up and whether the template bugs are fixed
